newsitem.title: GREECE: FOREX INFLOWS SHIFT GREEK FORWARD CURVE DOWN.
newsitem.headline: FOREX INFLOWS SHIFT GREEK FORWARD CURVE DOWN.

text.p: Greek short-term depos were trading lower in late dealings and forex forwards were softer across-the-board on mark and ecu selling from London-based players that strengthened the drachma, dealers said.
Trading activity remained subdued and bond prices were frozen in late trade, dealers said.
"Short-term depos fell after the central bank chose to leave liquidity unchanged," said a dealer at a private bank. "Long-term depos are little changed."
The Bank of Greece drained 100 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its depo tender. A facility of 100 billion drachmas was expiring today leaving system liquidity unchanged.
Forex forwards eased across-the-board with the drop more accentuated in short tenors on the heels of ecu and mark selling for drachmas from foreign players.

London-based banks sold a large amount of marks and smaller amounts of ecus for drachmas driving mark/drachma below 157 and pushing ecu/drachma lower to 309.37/42, off an intraday high of 309.82/87, dealers said.

"Mark/drachma pierced the 157 level on the downside after London-based players sold large amounts of marks for drachmas," a forex dealer said. "Ecu/drachma is also down, helped by some ecu selling and the selling of marks."
Bond prices were paralysed and trading activity remained thin, dealers said.

"There are inquiries but no price movement," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "But with yield spreads of Greek bonds over others widening, it is just a matter of time before we see foreign demand for Greek bonds emerging."
The mark was quoted at 156.90/00 from Wednesday's 157.960 fix, the dollar at 276.89/99 drachmas from 276.640 and the ecu at 309.21/31 from 309.47 drachmas.
